name: LaunchMyStore
tagline: Hosted ecommerce store builder: product catalog, checkout, and a storefront you do not have to deploy.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: A storefront is one of the most tutorialised things on the internet, so an agent will absolutely hand you a working product grid, cart, and Stripe Checkout flow in a session. What it will not hand you is the boring half: tax calculation by jurisdiction, chargeback and fraud handling, abandoned cart emails, inventory that stays honest under concurrent orders, and a payments relationship that survives your first refund dispute. If you sell five to fifty digital products to people who already know you, the DIY build is genuinely fine and cheaper forever. If you sell physical goods across borders, you are rebuilding an ops department, not a website. Verdict lands on kinda because the storefront is trivial and everything downstream of the buy button is not.
coreLoopDIY: A self-hosted Next.js storefront that reads a local product catalog, sends buyers to Stripe Checkout, and records paid orders in SQLite with a password-protected admin list.
requirements: A Stripe account with API keys (test mode works end to end)
A domain and somewhere to host a Node app
Product images and copy you supply yourself
Comfort reading Stripe webhook logs when an order does not appear
whatYouLose: Automatic sales tax and VAT calculation, plus the filing paperwork that follows
Fraud screening, dispute handling, and someone else's name on the merchant account
Themes, drag-and-drop editing, and a mobile-decent design you did not have to fight for
App ecosystem plumbing: shipping rates, print-on-demand, reviews, email flows
Uptime during a traffic spike, which is now entirely your problem
moatNotes: The storefront is a weekend. The payments, tax, and dispute surface underneath it is why hosted commerce keeps charging monthly.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the thing that costs money in ecommerce is never the product page. It is tax rules that change per state and per country, a checkout that has been A/B tested by someone else against millions of real buyers, and the fact that when a card is disputed the platform absorbs the process instead of emailing you a PDF. People also pay to not think about it: a store that goes down on launch day costs more than a year of subscription, and a hosted builder means a stranger is on call. For a hobby shop with a handful of digital goods, none of that is worth paying for. For anything with inventory, shipping, and real revenue, it is cheap.
notes: Fine DIY target for digital goods and a bad one the moment physical shipping and tax enter the picture.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted single-vendor storefront I can run on my own domain.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript and Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3 for orders, with a migration script
- Stripe Checkout (hosted) for payments, Stripe webhooks for order confirmation
- No user accounts for buyers, no analytics, no telemetry, no third-party fonts

In scope:
- Products defined in /content/products/*.md with frontmatter: title, slug, priceCents, currency, images, inventory (integer or "unlimited"), digitalFile (optional path)
- Home page product grid, product detail page, simple cart held in localStorage
- Checkout: POST /api/checkout builds a Stripe Checkout Session from cart line items, server-side price lookup only (never trust client prices)
- Webhook at /api/stripe/webhook verifying the signature, writing an order row (email, line items, amount, stripe session id) and decrementing inventory in a single transaction
- Digital delivery: for products with digitalFile, generate a signed one-time download link valid 24 hours, emailed via SMTP env vars
- /admin protected by a single ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env: list orders newest first, mark fulfilled, export CSV
- Seed 3 example products and a script to simulate a paid webhook locally

Out of scope, do not build:
- Tax or VAT calculation, shipping rate engines, discount codes, multi-currency
- Themes, page builder, drag-and-drop, or a CMS UI
- Subscriptions, marketplaces, or multiple vendors

All secrets in .env (STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, ADMIN_PASSWORD, SMTP_*), with .env.example committed and .env gitignored.
Write a README covering local setup, Stripe CLI webhook forwarding, and how to add a product.
Include a test that asserts server-side pricing ignores tampered client cart amounts.
